section.sectionSummaryBrief: Through engagement with Torah, one affects the world to become a vessel for G-dliness.
section.t: And behold, through engaging in Torah, one also affects the world so that it becomes a vessel for G-dliness.
For through the Torah having traveled and descended etc. until it became clothed in physical matters so that a person can grasp it in his thought, speech, and action,
through this one also draws down into the world.
For it is known
that the Ten Utterances with which the world was created
correspond to the Ten Commandments,
as it is brought in the Zohar
on the verse,
"Ten, ten the shekel for the holy shekel,"
and therefore through engaging in Torah
(the Ten Commandments)
one affects the Ten Utterances,
so that they too will be in the holy shekel.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The Ten Utterances and Ten Commandments are equivalent, each affecting the other, with man's service in the lower world impacting the higher realms.
section.t: And it can be said,
that this—that the Ten Utterances and the Ten Commandments are equivalent one opposite the other—
the intention in this is also that each one affects the other.
For just as the Ten Commandments affect
(as above)
the Ten Utterances,
and as the statement,
"He looked into the Torah and created the world,"
that the creation of the world is through the Ten Utterances as they are in the Torah,
which later descended in the aspect of "ordinary speech"
to bring the world into existence,
so too is it conversely,
that man's service in the matters of the world, which was created through the Ten Utterances of "ordinary speech," affects the Ten Commandments
[therefore there is an interpretation
in the Zohar's statement on the verse "Ten, ten" etc.,
that the Ten Utterances are higher than the Ten Commandments].
And it can be said that this is according to what is explained in Iggeret HaKodesh,
that the clarification of a law in Torah is specifically through a soul in a body,
and therefore the supernal ones come to hear novel Torah insights from the lower ones
(and as our sages said
on the verse,
"Friends hearken to your voice").
And to the extent that the Holy One, blessed be He, says to the ministering angels, "What are you asking Me? I and you will go to the court below."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Similarly, through the service of the bridegroom and bride below, additional light is drawn into their supernal counterparts, even in their highest root before the tzimtzum.
section.t: And so too is it with a bridegroom and bride,
that despite the fact that the bridegroom and bride below are derived from the aspect of bridegroom and bride above,
whose concept in the Sefiros is Zeir Anpin and Malchus,
and higher still, the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah
(bridegroom and bride)
are the matter of Ein Sof before the tzimtzum and the line, as explained at length in the discourses of my master, the Rebbe Maharash,
to the extent that the concept of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah is also before the tzimtzum,
nevertheless,
specifically through the service below
(and in particular through the joy of the bridegroom and bride below)
they draw additional light into the bridegroom and bride above, even as they are in their first root before the tzimtzum.
And in the manner that specifically through engaging in Torah and mitzvos below, the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah is effected,
as explained in Tanya,
even as they are supernal beyond supernal.
